claims.text: Linear's free plan costs $0 and allows unlimited members, but limits workspaces to 2 teams, 250 issues, and 10MB file uploads per file.
As of mid-2026, Linear Basic is listed at $10 per user per month when billed yearly.
As of mid-2026, Linear Business is listed at $16 per user per month when billed yearly.
Monthly billing costs more than yearly rates, with Basic listed at $12 per user per month and Business at $18 per user per month when billed monthly.
Linear's Basic plan was increased from $8 to $10 per user per month and Business from $14 to $16 per user per month between October 7 and November 12, 2025, both on annual billing.
A 20% discount is available on select plans when choosing annual billing.
Linear's free plan includes core issue tracking, projects, cycles, initiatives, customer requests, and the Linear Agent platform.
SAML single sign-on is available starting on the Business plan.
SCIM automated user provisioning is available on the Enterprise plan.
Enterprise adds audit logs, custom dashboards, sub-initiatives, HIPAA compliance with a BAA, and a dedicated account manager.
The Business plan adds private teams, guest access, and advanced AI features including Triage Intelligence and a CI/CD Releases integration.
Linear offers automatic issue linking from GitHub branches and pull request status updates back to issues, plus an MCP server for integrating with code and design environments.
Linear replaces traditional sprint ceremonies with Cycles and a continuous planning model.
Atlassian discontinued Jira Data Center products in favor of Atlassian Cloud, with Data Center support ending and cloud migration recommended.
Jira Data Center has been reported to start at $51,000 per year.
Height was described as a direct Linear competitor with a similar keyboard-first, opinionated workflow and AI features, offering paid plans from $6.99 per user per month.
Height is reported to have shut down on September 24, 2025.
ClickUp is identified as a leading alternative, offering a free plan and paid tiers ranging from $7 to $12 per user per month annually, plus an Enterprise plan with custom pricing.
Atlassian, the maker of Jira, acquired The Browser Company for $610 million.
Linear is considered best for software teams that value speed and modern AI features that come at no extra cost.
Linear is viewed as less customizable and too rigid for non-technical teams in sales, marketing, or HR.
Compared to Jira, Linear wins on speed, simplicity, and developer experience, while Jira wins on breadth, enterprise readiness, and customization.
Linear includes core AI agent features across all plans, whereas Jira's sprint automation depends more heavily on deployment type and Marketplace apps.
Linear offers tight GitHub integration with automatic issue linking from branches and PR status updates.
Across reviews, Linear was frequently described as fast, with users citing almost instant page loads and a keyboard-driven interface that stays out of the way.
Linear is praised for its speed, clean interface, and modern AI features included at no extra cost.
One pricing guide lists overall Linear plan costs ranging from $5,000 to $70,000 depending on organizational needs. (price $5,000 not found on the cited page)
Linear Enterprise uses custom annual pricing negotiated based on seat count and requirements. (judge: not_stated)
Linear integrates with third-party time tracking tools such as TrackingTime, Timely, and TMetric to add timers and timesheets inside the app. (judge: contradicted)

Jira is a primary competitor, with Cloud plans starting at $7.91 per user per month for Standard and $14.54 per user per month for Premium, plus an Enterprise tier with custom pricing. (judge: not_stated)
Fireship characterized Linear as the result of rebuilding issue tracking with modern UX principles, contrasting it with Jira's entrenched position in large organizations. (judge: not_stated)

ThePrimeagen stated that development teams should use tools like Linear or ClickUp, noting ClickUp is the closest option to Linear for teams that need project management beyond engineering. (judge: not_stated)
